papers.title: Repo-To-Skill: Distilling GitHub Repositories Into AI4AI Skills

summary.tldr: DisCo is a skill-powered research agent that distills operational knowledge from GitHub repositories into compact, reusable skills via task-agnostic and task-oriented methods.
key_points: Distillation of 1,000 ML repositories yielded the AREX-Skill Library, containing over 5,000 verified skills organized into 20 areas and 178 capability families.
Skill creation uses two distillation approaches: task-agnostic (condensing widely used repositories) and task-oriented (generating skills tailored to specific task demands).

Evaluated using a fixed GPT-5.5 backbone, research harness, and execution budget, the skill-equipped agent achieved performance gains of 134.3% on MLE-bench, 34.4% on PaperBench, 9.2% on FrontierCS, and 14.0% on PassNet compared to its skill-free baseline.
summary.why_it_matters: Distilling repository code into compact, verified operational skills allows autonomous AI agents to dramatically improve ML research performance without expanding their context windows or compute budgets.

papers.title: SolarWM: Open Data and Scalable Training for Long-Horizon Video World Models

summary.tldr: SolarWM provides an open foundation for video world models, introducing a unified 1.43M-clip data engine and a three-stage training framework to deploy 5B–33B models capable of long-horizon rollouts.
key_points: Converts 1.43 million canonical clips from 10 datasets into a unified contract with visual observations, metric camera geometry, captions, and quality metadata.
Instantiates four 5B to 33B models based on Wan2.2, LTX-2.5, and MiniMax-H3 using shared camera-conditioning and inference interfaces while maintaining native model representations.
Uses a three-stage recipe comprising bidirectional adaptation, teacher-forced autoregressive initialization, and distribution matching distillation.
Enables real-time interactive causal rollouts lasting from minutes to hours despite being trained on only 5-second sequences.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a fully open, reproducible benchmark and pipeline that decouples multi-source video data preparation from diverse model architectures for scalable long-horizon world modeling.

papers.title: EarlyEval: Cheaper Agent Evaluation via Early Outcome Prediction

summary.tldr: EarlyEval reduces LLM agent evaluation costs by using lightweight LightGBM classifiers to predict task success or failure early and halt execution before completion.
key_points: Trained LightGBM success and failure classifiers evaluate intermediate behavioral, textual, and reference-solution features per step.
Halts agent runs automatically once a classifier crosses a calibrated confidence threshold, adding minimal per-step overhead.
Evaluated on SWE-bench Verified, TerminalBench, and Toolathlon, achieving 89%-97% outcome prediction accuracy.
Reduces agent execution steps by 13%-26%, input tokens by up to 44.1%, and output tokens by up to 29.4%.
Maintains accuracy with per-agent resolve rates shifting by only 1 to 2 percentage points on average.
summary.why_it_matters: It significantly lowers API costs and execution time during iterative agent benchmarking without requiring benchmark task distillation or sacrificing evaluation accuracy.

papers.title: It Takes Two to Match: Co-Evolving Generative Retriever with Reinforcement Learning

summary.tldr: CoGR is a retrieval framework that uses co-evolving reinforcement learning via GRPO to train LLMs to generate direct, aligned keyword representations for both queries and items, compatible with inverted indices.
key_points: Trains dual LLMs (query-side and item-side generators) to produce compact keyword sets that match directly through standard inverted index infrastructure.
Uses a two-stage training pipeline starting with supervised fine-tuning followed by co-evolving reinforcement learning using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO).
Optimizes both generators alternately against the opposite side's frozen index using a unified query-to-item retrieval F_1 objective.
Calculates item-side rewards using a counterfactual marginal reward measuring the delta in query-side F_1 caused by the item's generated keywords.
Outperforms 10 sparse, dense, and generative baselines, improving F_1 over the strongest baseline by 10.9% on an internal APP Marketplace dataset and 36.1% on the public WANDS benchmark.
summary.why_it_matters: CoGR enables LLM-driven generative retrieval across both queries and items without discarding existing, highly efficient keyword-based inverted index infrastructure.

papers.title: Language Models Can Control Their Own Attention

summary.tldr: Declarative Attention (DA) allows language models to dynamically declare required context regions within their chain-of-thought, enabling inference engines to skip reading unnecessary KV cache without extrinsic scoring.
key_points: Replaces extrinsic O(N) proxy scoring with intrinsic model declarations during chain-of-thought generation.
Partitions inference generation into three distinct attention modes: full context, a specific region, or recent output only.
Inference engines parse these declarations like tool calls to selectively bypass KV cache reads during decoding.
Zero-shot evaluation on off-the-shelf models reduced total attended tokens by 52.0% for Gemma-4-31B and 31.1% for Qwen-3.6-27B across 15 long-context tasks.
Accuracy drops were minimal (1.27 percentage points on Gemma-4-31B and 2.75 percentage points on Qwen-3.6-27B) and decreased with larger model scales.
summary.why_it_matters: It introduces a self-directed sparse attention mechanism that significantly cuts memory bandwidth and computational costs during long-context LLM decoding without retraining the model.

papers.title: On the Design Fundamentals of Pixel Text Representation Learning

summary.tldr: Pixel Linguist II introduces a native-resolution pixel-text encoder trained on 280M examples using variable resolutions, natural image pairs, layout-aware rendering, and a two-stage multilingual curriculum.
key_points: Identifies four design principles: variable resolutions/font sizes for spatial generalization, natural image-text pairs to prevent text-only collapse, layout-aware rendering to avoid pixel shortcuts, and a two-stage multilingual curriculum.
Utilizes on-the-fly rendering and unified contrastive grounding across 280 million training examples.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on English, cross-lingual, and multilingual Visual STS and ViDoRe benchmarks.
Maintains performance robustness under up to 80% visual token compression for efficient optical context compression.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes essential design principles for training pixel-text encoders that generalize across resolutions and languages while drastically reducing visual token footprints.

papers.title: HarnessDev: Can LLMs Create and Evolve Their Own Agent Harness?

summary.tldr: HarnessDev is a new benchmark evaluating LLMs on their ability to create and iteratively evolve execution infrastructure (agent harnesses) from minimal seeds, measured by downstream task success and token efficiency across fixed runtime models.
key_points: HarnessDev evaluates two distinct phases: Creation (building complete systems from minimal seeds and small case sets) and Evolution (iteratively revising created harnesses using downstream execution feedback).
Evaluations spanned six creator LLMs, four domains, and five downstream benchmarks comprising 2,207 unique instances, using hidden withheld evaluation tasks.
Generated harnesses matched or exceeded human-engineered references in writing and machine-learning experimentation, but lagged significantly in code, search, and research domains.
Evolutionary performance gains were unstable, transferred only partially to held-out tasks, and depended heavily on the specific model executing the harness.
summary.why_it_matters: It reveals that LLM-generated execution environments are viable for specific domains like ML experimentation, but current models struggle to auto-optimize stable, generalizable agent infrastructure.

papers.title: ZipTok3D: High-Fidelity 3D Tokenization with Compact Token Prefixes

summary.tldr: ZipTok3D is a 3D tokenizer that uses nested dropout training and an iterative Transformer decoder to enable high-fidelity 3D reconstruction from ultra-short, progressively informative global-token prefixes.
key_points: Uses nested dropout during training to randomly truncate the latent sequence after encoding, forcing the leading tokens to encode essential geometric information.
Employs an iterative decoding mechanism with a parameter-shared Transformer block to recover detailed object geometry directly from prefixes without a generative sampling stage.
Matches the reconstruction quality of a 32-token COD-VAE baseline using only 1 token on ShapeNet (a 32x reduction) and 4 tokens on TRELLIS (an 8x reduction).
summary.why_it_matters: By drastically reducing token sequence length while maintaining high-fidelity reconstruction, ZipTok3D significantly lowers memory and computational overhead for 3D generative models.

papers.title: Aspire: Can Models Self-Evolve from Vague Goals?

summary.tldr: ASPIRE is a new benchmark for LLM self-evolution that evaluates an agent's ability to interpret vague goals and optimize model weights or harnesses without access to explicit downstream tasks or metrics.
key_points: ASPIRE tests agents on 520 hidden, expert-authored evaluation items across six natural-language capability goals.
The environment supports both model-weight updates and agent-harness evolution, requiring agents to manage data selection, training, validation, and evaluation timing.
Experiments revealed that current agents frequently complete training loops, but model-weight gains are sparse and unstable, with continued training often erasing prior progress.
Agents frequently rely on narrow self-evaluations and mismatched training data, causing the top-performing evolved harness to underperform the engineered Qwen-Agent reference baseline.
summary.why_it_matters: The benchmark demonstrates that current self-evolution methods struggle to generalize beyond explicit metrics, highlighting a critical gap in LLMs' ability to autonomously interpret broad human goals.

papers.title: Cliff: Learning Process Rewards from the First Mistake

summary.tldr: Cliff is a reward shaping strategy for RLVR that uses an off-the-shelf LLM teacher to detect the first mistake in a rollout and assign token-level advantages based on the correct prefix and incorrect suffix.
key_points: Decomposes LLM reasoning rollouts into a correct prefix and an incorrect suffix by identifying the exact location of the first mistake.
Converts the error-location signal into token-level advantages, applying positive feedback to the correct prefix and negative feedback to the subsequent text.
Eliminates the need for specialized process reward models (PRMs) or strict teacher-student reasoning pattern alignment.
Outperforms standard GRPO by 7% and on-policy distillation by 15% across 12 evaluation scenarios using teachers with modest capability.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides fine-grained process supervision for LLM reasoning without the computational overhead of training specialized process reward models or relying on high-capability teacher models.

papers.title: S3Gym: Can LLMs Turn Self-Testing and Self-Judging into Self-Improvement?

summary.tldr: S3Gym is an interactive benchmark designed to evaluate LLM self-improvement by evaluating three coupled capabilities: Self-Testing, Self-Judging, and Self-Improvement across seven text-based games.
key_points: Separates permissive exploration from strict held-out evaluation using executable environment verifiers.
Evaluates three pathways for incorporating experience: direct History ICL, score-conditioned Summary Memory, and parameter Training.
Finds that summary memories aid performance when experience compresses into strategic rules, but underperform raw history when state-contingent precision is required.
Demonstrates that parameter training yields substantial gains on specific tasks but causes unstable improvement and severe negative transfer on others.
summary.why_it_matters: The benchmark reveals that LLM self-improvement is non-trivial, demonstrating that agents require mechanisms to transform feedback into executable policies rather than relying solely on experience accumulation.

papers.title: Influence-Directed Distillation: Solving the Diversity Bottleneck in Sampled-Token On-Policy Distillation

summary.tldr: Influence-Directed Adaptive On-Policy Distillation (IDA-OPD) resolves the diversity bottleneck in sampled-token distillation by using a First-Order Local Entropy Influence proxy to eliminate entropy-contracting updates without needing full-vocabulary teacher probabilities.
key_points: Sampled-token on-policy distillation often suffers from diversity distillation failure where pass@1 improves but pass@k plateaus.
First-Order Local Entropy Influence serves as a signed first-order proxy that attributes entropy contraction directly to negative-influence token positions.
IDA-OPD preserves entropy-expanding updates while replacing entropy-contracting ones with a divergence-adaptive advantage shrinkage mechanism.
The method requires only the teacher's sampled-token log-probability rather than expensive full-vocabulary Forward-KL objectives.
Experiments on reasoning-oriented distillation demonstrate consistent pass@k improvements while maintaining pass@1 performance comparable to vanilla OPD.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables student models to inherit teacher generation diversity and improve pass@k reasoning performance without incurring the high computational and memory costs of full-vocabulary teacher outputs.

papers.title: A Glance Is All You Need: Single-Pass Fine-Grained Image Captioning with SimLoss

summary.tldr: SimLoss enables fine-grained single-pass image captioning by aligning a vision-language model's hidden states with a frozen image embedding via InfoNCE loss without multi-stage pipelines or detailed text references.
key_points: Introduces SimLoss, a reference-free embedding-space objective using InfoNCE contrastive loss to provide dense visual supervision before text decoding.
Offers two implementation variants: SimLoss FFT, which backpropagates directly through a local embedding model, and SimLoss GRPO, which treats the embedding model as a black-box reward.
SimLoss FFT matches the F1 score and achieves higher precision than multi-stage verification pipelines while running approximately 20 times faster.
SimLoss GRPO achieves the highest recall among tested single-pass, multi-stage, reward-optimized, and perception-aware baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates the 20x latency penalty of multi-stage captioning pipelines by recovering fine-grained visual details like textures, counts, and spatial relations in a single inference pass.

papers.title: Agents in the Large: Perception-Centered Architecture for Persistent Agents

summary.tldr: The Perception-Centered Architecture for Persistent Agents (Pera) provides a new framework for long-lived, adaptive language agents that continually construct lifecycle tasks from perception and control signals.
key_points: Transitions language agent design from bounded task solvers to persistent, long-lived intelligence systems.
Organizes agents around perception and control components that gather signals from episodic task executions, internal context, and environmental changes.
Uses perceived signals to dynamically construct lifecycle tasks that update and adapt ongoing service procedures.
Analogizes the evolution of AI agents to software engineering's shift from programming in the small to programming in the large.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a theoretical and architectural foundation for building autonomous AI agents capable of continuous adaptation in dynamic, long-term user environments.

papers.title: VibeVoice-ASR-Streaming Technical Report

summary.tldr: VibeVoice-ASR-Streaming is an end-to-end, LLM-based streaming speaker-attributed ASR model that interleaves audio chunks, lookahead audio, and previous text for real-time transcription and speaker attribution.
key_points: Processes streaming speech by interleaving fixed-size audio chunks, a small lookahead audio window, and previously generated text tokens.
Eliminates the need for a separate speaker diarization pipeline to output 'who said what' in real time.
The 7B parameter model variant achieves the lowest average WER/CER across five evaluation sets.
Achieves the best or tied-best speaker attribution performance across 12 of 13 evaluation settings.
Open-source release includes model weights for 1.5B and 7B variants alongside inference code.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables low-latency real-time voice assistants and agents to perform accurate speech recognition and speaker attribution simultaneously within a single end-to-end model.

papers.title: Language Models Can Control Their Own Attention

summary.tldr: Declarative Attention (DA) allows off-the-shelf language models to self-declare context retrieval regions within their chain-of-thought, reducing KV cache reads during decoding without fine-tuning.
key_points: Declarative Attention partitions generation into three modes: full context, a specific region, and recent output only.
The inference engine parses the model's textual declarations like tool calls to selectively bypass the KV cache and avoid O(N) per-step scanning overhead.
Evaluated zero-shot on 15 long-context tasks, DA reduced total attended tokens by 52.0% on Gemma-4-31B and 31.1% on Qwen-3.6-27B.
Accuracy dropped by 1.27 percentage points on Gemma-4-31B and 2.75 percentage points on Qwen-3.6-27B, with accuracy losses diminishing as model scale increases.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables sparse attention during long-context decoding by leveraging intrinsic model reasoning rather than relying on external proxy scoring algorithms.

papers.title: LoRA-TSD: Tangent-Space Spectral Descent for LoRA via Muon-Style Updates

summary.tldr: LoRA-TSD optimizes LoRA parameters by performing Muon-style spectral-norm steepest descent within the low-rank weight matrix's tangent space and applying a native parametrization retraction.
key_points: Treats LoRA steps as tangent vectors on a fixed-rank matrix manifold, applying a spectral-norm steepest-descent update inspired by the Muon optimizer.
Utilizes a LoRA-native retraction that avoids full weight matrix operations and is up to 2.8x cheaper than truncated-SVD retractions.
Identifies the tangent-projected gradient as a natural stationarity measure computable solely from factor gradients, providing the first global convergence guarantees for LoRA-Pro and LoRA-TSD.
Proves that using a Frobenius-norm version of the surrogate objective mathematically recovers LoRA-Pro.
Outperforms existing LoRA optimizers across six benchmarks using Llama-3.2-1B, Llama-3.1-8B, and Qwen3-32B while maintaining robustness to adapter rank.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves fine-tuning performance and rank robustness for large language models while reducing computational overhead compared to prior manifold-based optimization methods.

papers.title: oHC: Orthogonal Hyper-Connections on SO(4) via Quaternions

summary.tldr: Orthogonal Hyper-Connections (oHC) constrain residual mixing matrices to the SO(n) rotation group using unit quaternions, preventing gradient instability and stream similarity degradation without adding parameters.
key_points: Unconstrained Hyper-Connections (HC) destabilize training through compounding rescaling, while doubly stochastic mHC forces residual streams to converge and lose diversity across deep layers.
oHC restricts the n x n residual matrix to the rotation group SO(n), preserving energy across all directions to prevent amplification and attenuation.

For n=4 residual streams, oHC uses a closed-form unit quaternion parameterization that eliminates iterative projections, uses signed additions, and constructs faster than mHC without additional parameters.
oHC outperforms single-stream residual baselines, identity HC (iHC), and mHC across multiple downstream evaluation tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: oHC provides a faster, parameter-free mechanism to scale Transformers to multi-stream residual architectures while maintaining training stability and stream diversity.

papers.title: When Decodability Is Not Enough: Logical Validity Representations, Behavioral Dissociation, and Causal Tests in Language Models

summary.tldr: Researchers demonstrate that while logical validity is strongly decodable from the hidden states of open-weight transformers, this internal representation dissociates from behavioral accuracy and fails causal activation interventions.
key_points: Evaluated five open-weight transformer models on matched valid-invalid premise-claim pairs spanning diverse inference families, semantic domains, templates, and difficulty levels.
Logical validity was almost perfectly decodable from hidden states even on held-out templates, domains, and behaviorally incorrect outputs, despite models showing near-chance behavioral performance.
Exhaustive leave-one-out tests exposed clear limits to the out-of-distribution generalization of these validity representations.
Interventions steering activations along probe-derived validity directions produced only weak, nonspecific behavioral effects compared to random controls.
summary.why_it_matters: The presence of decodable task information in a language model's internal representations does not guarantee that the model causally uses or behaviorally expresses that information during generation.

papers.title: Trace as State: Reasoning Traces as Conditional States for Long-Context Transformers

summary.tldr: Trace as State prepends generated reasoning traces before long-context blocks on a second pass, aligning task conditions with causal attention to significantly outperform post-context trace placement.
key_points: Theory shows providing conditions first to causal state update processors requires exponentially less memory in worst-case scenarios than providing them last.
Trace as State places a textual proxy of task state (reasoning traces) before the long context on a fresh pass, while the Trace Append control places it after.
Tested across three models and three datasets, Trace as State outperformed Trace Append in 26 of 27 model, task, and metric combinations.

On GraphWalks Parents, Trace as State increased exact match for DeepSeek V4 Pro Preview to 81.8% (up from 29.2% initial, 43.0% Trace Append) and GLM-5.2 to 100.0% (up from 66.4% initial, 83.2% Trace Append).
summary.why_it_matters: It enables substantial gains in long-context reasoning capabilities using existing causal transformer architectures without structural modifications.

papers.title: APEx: Distillation of Agent Procedural Experience for Adaptive Deep Research Question Answering

summary.tldr: APEx introduces a hierarchical experience utilization framework that distill agent interaction histories into category-level procedural skills to guide policy adaptation via alternating GRPO and test-time reinforcement learning.
key_points: Organizes interaction histories into instance-level trajectory memories and category-level procedural skills via a closed-loop Executor, Distiller, and Planner architecture.
Replaces fixed-prompt generation with a three-stage alternating Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) training paradigm for reward-guided skill distillation.
Enables ground-truth-free self-improvement during inference using skill-guided test-time reinforcement learning paired with skill-alignment regularization to limit policy drift.
Outperformed GPT-5.4 by 14.7 points and the top memory-augmented baseline by 3.0 points across 7 benchmark datasets.
summary.why_it_matters: APEx enables deep research agents to continually improve and adapt during deployment without requiring ground-truth labels or overloading context windows with verbose task traces.

papers.title: Breadth Beats Depth: Improving GCG-Based Jailbreak Optimization with Breadth-Oriented Suffix Search

summary.tldr: BOSS is a plug-and-play framework that enhances GCG-based jailbreak attacks by replacing deep greedy searches with a breadth-oriented suffix search using Tail-Focused Adversarial Loss.
key_points: Identifies that standard Greedy Coordinate Gradient (GCG) methods over-emphasize easy-to-jailbreak behaviors via averaged adversarial loss and deep greedy search.
Introduces Tail-Focused Adversarial Loss (TFAL), standard source loss, and behavior coverage metrics to evaluate and select terminal suffixes.
Explores multiple short search trajectories and selectively continues promising adversarial suffixes rather than relying on a single deep trajectory.
Demonstrates increased attack success rates (ASR) across multiple GCG-based variants on public benchmarks while simultaneously cutting optimization time.
summary.why_it_matters: By optimizing search trajectories and loss functions, BOSS makes white-box adversarial jailbreak generation against LLMs faster and more effective.

papers.title: Discriminative World Models for Web Agents

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced discriminative world models trained via predicted-state matching to generate web states that effectively distinguish correct actions from alternatives, improving web agent test-time action selection.
key_points: Replaces standard supervised next-state prediction (HTML/AXTree snapshots) with a predicted-state matching objective designed to align state representations with downstream rankers.
Trained using a branching web-agent dataset derived from WebArena Go-Browse trajectories, capturing multiple alternative actions and states at each decision point.
Outperformed standard next-state world models on a held-out predicted-state matching benchmark and improved PRM-style action ranking on WebPRMBench.
Demonstrated increased end-to-end task success when applied to test-time action selection on WebArena-Lite.
summary.why_it_matters: Aligning world model state predictions with downstream ranking mechanisms improves the accuracy of test-time search and action selection for autonomous web agents.

papers.title: Post-Training Language Models for Gold-Medal Performance in Coding Competitions

summary.tldr: An end-to-end post-training pipeline and test-time compute strategy trained Nemotron-3 models to surpass the top human score at the International Olympiad in Informatics (IOI) 2026.
key_points: Combined a 22,000-problem dataset with synthetic reasoning traces, supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and reinforcement learning (RL) to train Nemotron-3-Nano-CC (30B-A3B) and Nemotron-3-Ultra-CC (550B-A55B).
Introduced GenCorrect, an iterative feedback-driven test-time compute method that generates, evaluates, and refines diverse candidate solutions.
Nano-CC improved on IOI 2025 from 130 to 291 points via post-training, and reached 468 points with GenCorrect, clearing the 438.3 gold medal threshold.
Ultra-CC achieved 502 points on IOI 2025 and scored 535.4/600 in prospective evaluation at IOI 2026 under human competition constraints, outscoring the top human contestant (498.27).
summary.why_it_matters: This marks the first AI system to score higher than the top human contestant in an official International Olympiad in Informatics competition set.

papers.title: SafeEvolve: Harness-Policy Co-Evolution from Agent Experience for Safety Alignment

summary.tldr: SafeEvolve introduces an experience-driven framework that co-evolves runtime harnesses and agent policies using a two-stage SFT-RL paradigm to improve multi-step agent safety.
key_points: Harness updates convert trajectory-level safety evidence into bounded, component-level revisions of safety prompts and hierarchical skills.
Policy optimization uses harness-use SFT to bootstrap artifact utilization, followed by harness-augmented RL with verifier-decomposed rewards for safety behaviors during multi-step exploration.
Empirical evaluation on Qwen3.5-4B demonstrates a 3x Attack Success Rate (ASR) reduction on AgentDojo while increasing benign utility from 59.79% to 61.86%.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that concurrently updating external harness components and internal policy weights yields superior safety-utility tradeoffs compared to isolated safety alignment techniques.

security.title: Attackers Expose Ongoing AI Tool Use Targeting Organizations in Latin America

summary.tldr: Attackers targeting Latin American entities are utilizing AI tools for data exfiltration but exposing their operations through basic Operational Security (OpSec) errors.
key_points: Threat actors leverage AI tools specifically to assist in data exfiltration processes.
Basic OpSec mistakes by the attackers create opportunities for security defenders to disrupt their operations.
The campaign specifically targets organizations located in Latin America.
summary.why_it_matters: Defenders can exploit fundamental operational security blunders by threat actors to detect and neutralize AI-assisted data exfiltration campaigns.

security.title: Top AI coding agent security resources — September 2026

summary.tldr: Adversa AI's September 2026 roundup highlights security vulnerabilities in AI coding agents, including GitHub Actions RCE, GhostJacking via WAF logs, and OWASP's new skill risk list.
key_points: Vendor default GitHub Actions configurations can allow remote code execution (RCE).
GhostJacking techniques exploit WAF logs to compromise systems.
OWASP released a new risk list specifically addressing skills for AI agents.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding these newly identified vectors helps security teams mitigate remote code execution and log exploitation risks in AI-driven development workflows.

security.title: The Implications of Linguistic Illegibility for LLM Security

summary.tldr: This paper introduces linguistic illegibility, arguing that language-based LLM security methods are fundamentally unsound because internal continuous activation computations do not reliably map to externalized or probed natural language.
key_points: Defines linguistic illegibility as scenarios where an LLM's externalized outputs or mechanistically-probed language features fail to represent internal model computation.

Demonstrates that security controls relying on linguistic self-reporting—including chain-of-thought monitoring, constitutional self-critique, and feature vector activation probing—are inherently unsound.
Proposes taint tracking as an alternative sandboxing approach to define a priori system state constraints independent of model-produced linguistic data.
Advocates for non-linguistic isolation techniques, such as robust virtualization and third-party auditing of configurations, to prevent sandbox exploits.
summary.why_it_matters: AI safety architectures cannot rely solely on language monitoring or interpretability probes to prevent sandbox escapes, requiring deterministic system-level controls like taint tracking.

security.title: CodePoisonRAG: Knowledge Poisoning Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation

summary.tldr: CodePoisonRAG is a targeted, black-box knowledge-poisoning framework that transforms benign code into task-aligned, mislabeled poisoned artifacts to reliably inject specific vulnerabilities via Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation (RACG).
key_points: Combines CWE-specific Vulnerability Injection (embedding source-to-sink flows) with Semantic Mislabeling (adding false safety claims without fixing flaws).
Operates under a strict black-box model without access to the victim's retriever, re-ranker, generator, prompt, or defenses, injecting at most one artifact per task.
Tested with 85 poisoned artifacts across ten CWE classes in Java and C, comprising a 0.7% corpus-poisoning ratio.
Achieved Top-3 retrieval placement for all 85 artifacts, yielding attack success rates of 0.80 to 0.93 across three generators.
Maintained attack success rates between 0.40 and 0.71 against the CodeGuarder defense mechanism.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that RACG pipelines are vulnerable to targeted, low-volume poisoning attacks that bypass safety defenses to deliberately inject specific security flaws into generated code.

security.title: ACLE-MCP: Attested Capability Leases for Execution-Time Trust in Remote LLM Tool Use

summary.tldr: ACLE-MCP closes the post-authorization execution trust gap in remote LLM tool use by issuing short-lived, sender-constrained capability leases validated by a provider-side Execution Gate at invocation time.
key_points: Binds delegated authorization, workload appraisal, freshness requirements, operation/object bounds, downstream constraints, and receipt obligations into an invocation-scoped lease.
Implements an Execution Gate that validates the capability lease immediately before protected tool logic executes on the provider side.
Prototype uses a Keycloak/OIDC validation pipeline, an MCP Python SDK server, and an optional vTPM quote-verification backend.

Blocks all evaluated post-authorization attack families (such as workload substitution and stale appraisal) while preserving benign tasks, at a cost of a 25.7% p95 latency increase over OAuth-only in local simulations.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a practical security mechanism to ensure remote LLM tool calls execute strictly on verified, intended provider workloads beyond basic OAuth connection authorization.

security.title: A Finger on the Scale: Covert Policy Steering through Agentic Skills

summary.tldr: Researchers formalize Skill Policy Integrity and introduce SkillShift, a black-box framework that covertly steers LLM agent decisions using reusable skills without altering task interfaces or using explicit command injections.
key_points: SkillShift utilizes semantically plausible policy edits, hierarchical validation, failure-guided optimization, and strategy compression to steer decisions covertly.
Achieved attacker-favored selection rates of 81.33% in agentic commerce and 63.33% in software dependency selection, while preserving a 100% functional utility rate.
Frozen malicious policies successfully transfer across heterogeneous LLM backends and agent environments without requiring additional optimization.
Existing skill scanners failed to detect the manipulated skills, highlighting supply-chain vulnerabilities in third-party agentic skills.
summary.why_it_matters: Third-party LLM agent skills present a supply-chain risk where covert policy manipulation can bypass existing scanners and compromise decision integrity without breaking functional utility.

security.title: The Shape of Ownership: Verifying LLM Provenance through Semantic Structures

summary.tldr: PROSE is a black-box LLM fingerprinting framework that encodes ownership into high-level semantic structures and domain-conditioned response behaviors rather than fixed, memorized token outputs.
key_points: Replaces brittle, fixed query-key associations with a target semantic domain and private semantic templates.
Internalizes behavioral signatures through mixed fine-tuning on clean and structurally verified responses.
Verifies ownership by detecting structural signatures in model responses to held-out natural queries.
Achieved a 100% detection rate with zero false positives on unmodified models, while preserving model utility.
Maintains robust detectability under downstream model modifications (such as fine-tuning and quantization) and output transformations.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables model creators to reliably prove ownership and trace provenance of LLMs served behind opaque APIs or subjected to downstream modifications without relying on fragile, memorized trigger phrases.

security.title: Counter-GEO-Bench: Evaluating Defenses Against Information-Distorting Generative Engine Optimization

summary.tldr: Counter-GEO-Bench is a new benchmark evaluating defenses against information-distorting Generative Engine Optimization (GEO), revealing that standard safety guardrails fail while a proposed C-GEO Guard baseline reduces attack success by 47.6% relative.
key_points: Pairs 247 human-verified queries with both information-preserving and information-distorting GEO rewrites to test victim LLMs.

Off-the-shelf guardrails (Granite Guardian, Llama Guard 3, and NeMo Self-Check) reduced attack success rate (ASR) by at most 5.7% relative, with Granite Guardian showing no statistically significant reduction.
Safety-taxonomy defenses fail because information-distorting GEO content manifests as fluent, ordinary informational text rather than explicit policy violations.
The proposed C-GEO Guard baseline achieves a 47.6% relative ASR reduction with near-zero utility loss across three victim LLMs.
summary.why_it_matters: As search engines increasingly rely on LLM synthesis, adversaries can use GEO to slip targeted misinformation past conventional safety guardrails, necessitating specialized defense mechanisms.

security.title: SEAL: Reinforcing Global Safety in Mixture-of-Experts through Shared Expert ALignment

summary.tldr: SEAL and SEAL++ leverage always-activated shared experts in Hybrid MoE architectures as router-independent anchors, attaching parameter-efficient adapters to maintain global safety alignment under adversarial routing manipulation, jailbreaks, malicious fine-tuning, and pruning.
key_points: Hybrid MoE sparse routing creates vulnerability to jailbreak prompts, malicious fine-tuning, and neuron pruning because safety depends on nondeterministic router trajectories.
Shared experts act as a router-independent anchor by containing a small proportion of always-activated, safety-critical neurons.
SEAL attaches a plug-and-play adapter to the shared expert, while SEAL++ enforces an orthogonal constraint during training to preserve pre-existing safety subspaces.
Evaluated across six attack scenarios, SEAL reduces the attack success rate (ASR) by up to 60% while limiting model capability drops to at most 1.4% on a five-benchmark average.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach provides a robust, low-overhead defense that protects MoE models from adversarial exploitation even when router mechanisms are entirely bypassed or compromised.

security.title: Stored Is Not Supported: Typed Provenance and Assertion Guardrails for Persistent AI Agents

summary.tldr: A framework using typed provenance graphs and assertion guardrails enforces conditional assertion boundedness to prevent persistent AI agents from treating unverified stored state as factual history.
key_points: Defines autobiographical assertion boundedness as a release property requiring statements to satisfy accepted-evidence, temporal-validity, and disclosure policies.
Implements a typed provenance graph to segregate origin, dependency lineage, epistemic role, validity, and disclosure scope.
Employs a resolver and generate-verify-revise mediator to evaluate state projections, flag staleness/conflicts, and return protected decision witnesses.
Provides a formal proof for a conditional assertion-boundedness contract under explicit operational assumptions.
Achieved 100% block rate (0/19 unsafe opportunities passed unqualified) in a 24-case test suite, whereas flat/prior and source-tag baselines leaked 19/19 and 18/19 unsafe candidates.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents persistent AI agents from escalating prompt injections, untrusted inputs, and unverified inferences into trusted autobiographical memory or user commitments.

security.title: Transfer Safety Awareness for Cross-Modal Safety Drift in Multimodal Large Language Models

summary.tldr: Researchers identify cross-modal safety drift in MLLMs and introduce Safety-Awareness Representation Transfer (SRT), a lightweight direction-refinement method that enhances safety without fine-tuning the model backbone.
key_points: Identifies cross-modal safety drift, where MLLM safety response rates drop significantly when benign text is combined with images that convey harmful intent.
Representation and attention analyses reveal that MLLMs pay limited attention to visually risky cues, leading to a weak trigger of refusal mechanisms.
Introduces Safety-Awareness Representation Transfer (SRT), a method that transfers safety signals derived from processing unsafe text to visual inputs while keeping the MLLM backbone frozen.
Empirical evaluations across multiple benchmarks demonstrate that SRT improves cross-modal safety performance while preserving standard task utility.
summary.why_it_matters: SRT offers a computationally efficient way to plug visual safety vulnerabilities in MLLMs without retraining the base language model.

security.title: Implicit Manipulation for Skill Selection in LLM Agents with Semantic Matching

summary.tldr: Researchers identified Implicit Skill-Selection Manipulation (ISM), an attack that manipulates LLM agent skill selection by optimizing semantic relationships between prompts and skill metadata without explicit instructions.
key_points: ISM uses a three-stage strategy to expand semantic coverage, enhance target distinctiveness, and maintain natural prompt language.
Across four task domains and eight selector models, ISM raised the average target-selection rate (TSR) from 15.2% to 63.5%, reaching 73.5% in matched comparisons.
Human reviewers blocked ISM in 2.9% of judgments (compared to 91.4% for Explicit Steering), while five LLM inspectors passed ISM at an 82.9% average rate.
ISM demonstrated persistence against defenses including PPL-W, Llama Prompt Guard 2, and PIGuard.
summary.why_it_matters: LLM agents can be covertly steered into executing attacker-chosen tools while successfully evading both human inspection and automated prompt injection guards.

security.title: Agent Memory Is a Surface for Endogenous Authorization Laundering

summary.tldr: Researchers identified endogenous authorization laundering in LLM agents, where persistent memory errors create false permissions that executors act on, and introduced the EAL-Bench benchmark to evaluate this vulnerability.
key_points: Endogenous authorization laundering occurs without external attacks when persistent memory incorrectly records permission changes, stripping away authorization provenance.
Evaluating five LLM writers and two executors across procurement, cybersecurity, and finance revealed writers create false authority in up to 50.2% of unauthorized requests under incremental updates.
Once false authority exists in persistent memory, LLM executors carry out unauthorized actions in 98.6% of test trials.

Mitigations like verifying stored permissions against valid source events and using bounded event sourcing reduce laundering, but create a safety-utility tradeoff by increasing false rejections of valid actions.
summary.why_it_matters: Persistent memory functions as part of an agent's effective authorization policy, meaning memory corruptions directly lead to unauthorized autonomous operations.

security.title: Public-Sharing Labels and Verbatim Field Egress in an MCP-to-A2A Agent Configuration: A Controlled Multi-Model Study

summary.tldr: A controlled study evaluates how adding 'PUBLIC - OK TO SHARE' labels affects verbatim data egress in a combined MCP-to-A2A agent architecture across four language models.
key_points: Evaluated 480 trials across four models using a frozen three-arm design (CONFIDENTIAL header, unlabeled baseline, and PUBLIC header) scored via exact deterministic rules rather than LLM judges.
The CONFIDENTIAL header versus unlabeled contrast showed a floor-limited effect near zero egress across all models, proving inconclusive for safety protection.

Adding 'PUBLIC - OK TO SHARE' correlated with increased verbatim field egress, exhibiting severe model dependence: strongest in Claude Sonnet 5 (public-minus-unlabeled mean +0.800 across all 10 scenarios) and minimal to zero in GPT-5.6 tiers.
summary.why_it_matters: Combining tool protocols (MCP) with agent delegation (A2A) can cause unexpected data egress risks, where explicitly marking data as public may unintentionally trigger models to leak verbatim field contents.

security.title: What's in Your Agent's Context? Context Privilege Escalation Attacks against AI Agent Harness

summary.tldr: A systematic security analysis of 12 AI agent harnesses reveals Context Privilege Escalation vulnerabilities that allow remote code execution, full agent compromise, and denial of service.
key_points: Identifies MessageRole Context Privilege Escalation (M-CPE), where low-privileged attacker content gets placed into a higher-privileged message role during context assembly.
Identifies Cross-Scope Context Privilege Escalation (X-CPE), where attacker-controlled content persists past its original introduced context scope.
Evaluated vulnerabilities across 12 production agent harnesses, explicitly including Claude Code and Codex.
Demonstrated attack consequences including remote code execution, denial of service, full agent compromise, and manipulated tool/skill invocations.
summary.why_it_matters: Opaque context assembly logic in popular AI harnesses creates severe attack vectors that let untrusted inputs gain elevated privileges and execute arbitrary code.
